{{2006 Winter Olympics}}
The [[2006 Winter Olympics]], officially known as the XX Olympic Winter Games, was a winter [[multi-sport event]] held in [[Turin]], [[Italy]], from February 10 to 26, 2006. A total of 2,508 athletes representing 80 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) (+3 from [[2002 Winter Olympics medal table|2002 Olympics]]) participated in 84 events (+6 from 2002) from 15 different [[Olympic sports#Winter Olympics|sports and disciplines]] (unchanged from 2002).<ref name="olympic.org">{{cite web|title = Turin 2006|publisher = International Olympic Committee|url = http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Turin-2006/|access-date = May 5, 2008|archive-date = July 5, 2014|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140705173501/http://www.olympic.org/en/content/Olympic-Games/All-Past-Olympic-Games/Winter/Turin-2006|url-status = live}}</ref>

Athletes from 26 NOCs won at least one medal, and athletes from 18 of these NOCs secured at least one gold.<ref name="olympic.org"/> [[Germany at the 2006 Winter Olympics|Germany]] won the highest number of gold medals (11) and led in overall medals (29) for the third consecutive Games. [[Latvia at the 2006 Winter Olympics|Latvia]] and [[Slovakia at the 2006 Winter Olympics|Slovakia]] won the first medals in their Winter Olympic history.<ref>{{cite news |title = Germany, U.S. finish 1-2, many nations share wealth in Turin medals race |publisher = [[ESPN]] |url = https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=oly&id=2345562 |date = February 26, 2006 |agency = Associated Press |access-date = May 6, 2008 |archive-date = October 24, 2012 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121024111802/http://sports.espn.go.com/espn/wire?section=oly&id=2345562 |url-status = live }}</ref>

[[Speed skating at the 2006 Winter Olympics|Speed skater]] [[Cindy Klassen]] of [[Canada at the 2006 Winter Olympics|Canada]] won five medals (one gold, two silver and two bronze) and was the most medalled athlete at the Games. [[Biathlon at the 2006 Winter Olympics|Biathlete]] [[Michael Greis]] of Germany and [[Short track speed skating at the 2006 Winter Olympics|short track speed skaters]] [[Ahn Hyun Soo]] and [[Jin Sun-Yu]], both of [[South Korea at the 2006 Winter Olympics|South Korea]], tied for the most gold medals, with three each.<ref>{{cite news |title = Great Olympic performances |publisher = [[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |url = https://www.cbc.ca/sports/2.722/great-olympic-performances-1.586694 |date = February 28, 2006 |access-date = May 5, 2008 |archive-date = September 24, 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080924191203/http://www.cbc.ca/sports/story/2006/02/28/oly_greatperformers060228.html |url-status = live }}</ref>

==Changes in medal standings==
{{see also|List of stripped Olympic medals}}
One athlete was stripped of an Olympic medal during these Games.<ref>{{cite web |title = 2006–Winter Olympics Games XX (Torino, Italy) |publisher = [[The Sports Network]] |url = https://www.tsn.ca/olympics/feature/?fid=10298 |access-date = May 5, 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080923214436/http://www.tsn.ca/olympics/feature/?fid=10298 |archive-date = September 23, 2008 |url-status = dead }}</ref> [[Russia at the 2006 Winter Olympics|Russian]] biathlete [[Olga Pyleva]] won a silver medal in the 15&nbsp;km race, but tested positive for [[carphedon]] and lost her medal. Germany's [[Martina Glagow]] was given the silver medal and fellow Russian [[Albina Akhatova]] (who was caught doping in 2009<ref>{{cite news |author= <!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2009/02/13/sports/13iht-dope.1.20176190.html |title= Biathlon champion is banned |work= [[The New York Times]] |date= November 3, 2009 |access-date= January 23, 2020 |archive-date= November 29, 2020 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20201129154942/https://www.nytimes.com/2009/02/13/sports/13iht-dope.1.20176190.html |url-status= live }}</ref> and missed the [[2010 Winter Olympics|2010 Olympics]]) won the bronze.<ref>{{cite news |title = Russian athlete stripped of medal |publisher = [[British Broadcasting Corporation|BBC Sports]] |url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/other_sports/winter_sports/4719916.stm |date = February 16, 2006 |access-date = May 5, 2008 |archive-date = February 21, 2009 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090221012033/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/other_sports/winter_sports/4719916.stm |url-status = live }}</ref>
===IOC retesting===
The IOC has retested nearly 500 doping samples that were collected at the 2006 Turin Games. In 2014, the Estonian Olympic Committee was notified by the IOC that a retested sample from cross-country skier [[Kristina Šmigun]] had tested positive. On October 24, 2016, the [[World Anti-Doping Agency]] Athletes' Commission stated that Šmigun, who won two gold medals at the Turin Games, would face a [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] hearing before the end of October.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1042965/smigun-vahi-facing-cas-hearing-after-positive-retest-at-turin-2006|title=Šmigun-Vähi facing CAS hearing after "positive" retest at Turin 2006|work=INSIDETHEGAMES.BIZ|first=Nick|last=Butler|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016|publisher=Dunsar Media Company Limited|archive-date=October 25, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161025115726/http://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1042965/smigun-vahi-facing-cas-hearing-after-positive-retest-at-turin-2006|url-status=live}}</ref> In December 2017, IOC announced that re-analysis of samples resulted in no positive cases.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1059102/estonian-cross-country-skier-looks-to-be-in-clear-as-ioc-announce-no-positive-results-in-turin-2006-re-analysis|title=Estonian cross-country skier looks to be in clear as IOC announce no positive results in Turin 2006 re-analysis|date=December 13, 2017|website=www.insidethegames.biz|first=Nick|last=Butler|access-date=March 23, 2022|archive-date=February 21, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220221173207/https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1059102/estonian-cross-country-skier-looks-to-be-in-clear-as-ioc-announce-no-positive-results-in-turin-2006-re-analysis|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Medal table==
{{see also|Olympic medal table}}
The medal table is based on information provided by the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |date=11 August 2024 |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |access-date=12 August 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |date=18 August 2008 |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |access-date=25 July 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |date=10 August 2024 |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |access-date=11 August 2024 |work=[[Diario AS]] |language=en-us}}</ref>
